flawed_step: The proof cannot justify the essential inference that being simultaneously 3-connected, cubic, and bipartite forces a spanning cycle; those hypotheses do not imply Hamiltonicity.
counterexample: The Horton graph is a concrete counterexample: it has 96 vertices and 144 edges, is finite and simple, is cubic, has a bipartition with 48 vertices in each part, and has vertex-connectivity 3 (so deleting any two vertices leaves it connected), yet it has no Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary: The universal statement is false. The proof attempt stops at the claimed implication from the three stated graph properties to Hamiltonicity, which is directly contradicted by the Horton graph.
